title: Convertible
text: “You guys…”
“For Shion and Wolf, that route works—sunglasses, an aloha shirt, driving a flashy convertible—it’d really pop, I say…”
“Vof.”
Wolf gave a firm thumbs-up and grinned.
“What’s a ‘convertible’?”
“A car with no roof! In carriage terms, it’d be like a cart, kyu!”

“In this world, if you look around Shieldfreeden, you can find cars designed by Takt or past heroes that fit the bill—though there aren’t many, what with the roads, maintenance, and production costs.”
“I get the idea, but is it cool? I know what an aloha shirt is—I saw one on Cal Mira Island. That’s the one you tried putting on me, right?”
“It’s an outfit that suits a muscular macho type, yeah.”

Father had put one on Crocodile Guy back on the island. So I quickly sketched a rough picture of Crocodile Guy and company tearing down the road in a convertible. As a bonus, once I added sunglasses, it turned into a picture of two villainous, muscular beastmen driving a convertible. Well, at least the general vibe should come across, I say.
“Yeah, yeah, exactly like this. Seriously, Shion and Wolf can totally pull off the wild look, so they’ve got the edge when it comes to the ‘American’ aesthetic.”
“Vof, looks like a villain.”
“Well, I suppose the character comes through?”
Wolf and Crocodile Guy nodded in agreement with Father’s assessment of the picture.
“This is outrageous! Are you saying I’m not cool, Iwatani-sama?!”
“Well, Teo, as you can see from Motoyasu-kun right now, you’re more the cute rabbit type, so…”
There’s a right fit and a wrong fit for everyone, kyu!

“To make you look cool, you’d probably need an eyepatch, messier hair, more visible muscle showing through—though if you get too buff, that’s gross in its own way, so there’s a balance needed… but yeah, an overly-muscled Teo would admittedly be a bit much.”
“Guh… ahem. Being cute is my charm, Iwatani-sama. To begin with, I only look after Bow Hero out of necessity—I’m not chasing ‘cool.’ Same goes for Bow Hero.”

“True, the current Itsuki doesn’t care about that stuff. He’s a pure efficiency-and-visibility guy through and through. That’s why his mostly-black outfit doesn’t clash too badly even with Kuro-chan’s mobile-carriage design…”
“Don’t drag that back up. Fine, I get it. As long as I’m in demi-human form while riding, that should be fine, right? Please redraw it.”
“That’s for me to decide, kyu.”
“This man…!”

Rabbit Guy’s protests were quite noisy, I say. Designing something Kuro-chan would actually like is tricky—the riders, namely Itsuki and company, give off way too much of a “foreign object” vibe. So, left with no choice, I drew Kuro-chan playing the engine role, tearing down the road as a sleek mobile carriage with Itsuki riding on top, while Rabbit Guy and the others rode along in a sidecar.
“Ah, that kind of vibe. A big motorcycle with a sidecar carrying an animal—yeah, that actually looks pretty picturesque.”
“How about something like this instead?”
I redrew it so that only Itsuki rode the Kuro-chan-based motorcycle, while Rabbit Guy ran alongside on all fours.
“I got kicked off?! Running on all fours chasing after them—what is that supposed to be?! Where’s Rishia-san in this?!”
“Right here, kyu.”
And there was Riska, trussed up and being dragged along like a prisoner on parade.
“Whoa… that’s harsh. It’s basically a gag now. And somehow Teo’s got this sharp, determined look running alongside, making him look cool.”
“Don’t try to make it funny! Besides, this is clearly you, isn’t it?!”
“I’m not this big, kyu.”
I’ve been researching a spell to turn into a giant usaunny in order to seduce Father, but it’s not going well, I say.
“Can we please stop watching Spear Hero’s doodles at some point?”
“Right. Motoyasu-kun, are you drawing over there?”
“Vof… want me to have him draw in my room?”
“As long as we can move around, no problem, indeed. Yuki-chan, let’s think it over together later.”
“Yes, ma’am!”
I recited Fairy Morph again and reverted from usaunny back to human form.
“Somehow we got sidetracked by Motoyasu-kun’s doodling. What were we even talking about?”
“Vof, the library-like dungeon thing? We were talking about stories and legends. My old room has a lot of books—want to check out the study?”
“Sure.”
“Got it. This way.”
And so we ended up heading to the study in Wolf’s castle-like mansion.
“This is the study.”
Upon arriving at the study… it turned out to be a room with a fairly decent collection of books. The shelves had quite a few gaps between the books that were there.
“The missing ones are in my room.”
“Seems like Wolf read a lot, huh.”
“Yeah.”
Wolf was clearly proud to be known as a well-read type, I say.
“Stories from another world, huh… I wonder what kind of tales are common. Well, I suppose hero stories get passed down as legends… no, wait, wouldn’t it be more accurate to call it religion?”
“Apparently, in this world’s stories—especially fairy tales—princes and princesses often show up as the heroes. Something like a reward for a protagonist who worked hard, indeed.”
Both Wolf and Rabbit Guy nodded at my answer.
“Lots of stories where everything gets resolved when someone’s in trouble.”
“So the hero is a convenient, wish-fulfillment prince, huh…”

Father’s remark could certainly be taken as rather cutting. Come to think of it, the Crimson Swine herself was unreasonable, and from a reincarnator’s perspective, precisely the kind of overly-convenient existence that fit “wish fulfillment.” And it was Father who ultimately claimed victory over her. In a sense, Father truly was, in the proper storybook sense, both the prince and the hero.
“…Vof, right. A hero is… the ultimate hero who saves the protagonist from unreasonable hardship. I’m certain of that. I was the one who got saved.”
Wolf knelt down, took Father’s hand, pressed it to his forehead, and prayed.
“…Yeah. From Wolf’s perspective, we really did help him out when he was struggling with all sorts of things, huh.”
It made for quite a picture, but something about it left me feeling weirdly unsettled, I say!
“Hmph…”
“What are you being so dramatic for?”
Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy cut in right there to point it out.
“I’m a hero too, I say! Riding in dashingly on Yuki-chan the white Filolial—now that’s a cool position, indeed.”
Apparently, showing up riding a white horse or a white Filolial was the classic pattern for princes and heroes.
“When Motoyasu-kun keeps quiet, he’s actually pretty cool. He did help me out too.”
“Indeed, I say!”
“Indeed, ma’am!”
Heh heh! Do you all understand? It is I who saves Father, I say.
“What’s this guy so smug about…”
“Still, honestly… now that I think about it again, there really is this sense of being inside a story, being around Iwatani-sama and everyone.”
“Can’t deny that.”
“That goes for me too, as a hero… we’ve run into some pretty awful developments along the way.”
“Vof. Speaking of which, do you two know about the rumor spreading around Siltvelt—Shion, Eclair?”
“Something come up?”
Wolf turned to Crocodile Guy, seeming to have something on his mind.
“The one about heroes fighting each other with Eclair as the prize.”
“Ah.”
“I heard some noble ladies in Siltvelt are jealous, saying it’s too extravagant. If Eclair’s ever headed to Siltvelt, she should watch out for harassment.”
“I see. True, usually it’s stories about fighting over a hero, so this is the reverse, isn’t it. That is rather extravagant.”
Oh? Is it extravagant?

“That’s true indeed… well, Lady Eclair doesn’t seem to intend on pursuing romance with Shield Hero, so if she states that firmly, there probably won’t be any harassment. Besides, Wolf, with your authority behind her, nothing too strange is likely to happen.”
“I won’t let anything like that happen, but it’s good to have that rumor in your ears just in case. Vof.”
“Indeed, protecting oneself is important. Even I, in a different loop, once had poison slipped to me and Yuki-chan and the others.”
“Whoa… I figured, but that’s still an unpleasant story. I see, huh… so that’s how it gets told on this side—as a duel dramatic enough to inspire jealousy.”
At that, the slaves all nodded together in agreement.
